rationale: Data: 6,766 works, each with 1 passage, all dated. Split at year 1876: 752 early and 6,014 late works across 8 genres. Rate = count__domains__DISTANCE_TRAVEL / n_passages. Estimand: take the mean rate across works within each genre-period cell, compute late minus early per genre, and average the 8 genre differences with equal weight. Result: +0.0021. A stratified bootstrap (2,000 resamples of works within each genre x period cell) gives a 95% CI of [-0.022, 0.025], which includes zero. Genre differences point in different directions. Adventure, domestic realist, juvenile and romance fall slightly; other and sensation/mystery rise; collection and historical barely change. The early cells are small (40-254 works). Robustness checks: high date-confidence works only give +0.003. Excluding works within 10 years of the cutoff gives -0.005. By origin, UK gives -0.017, US -0.024 and unknown +0.026, so the sign depends on the subset. Decade means fall from the very sparse early 1800s to a low in the 1870s-80s, then rise again, with no clear break at 1876. Possible alternative explanations for any apparent difference: genre mix and sample size change across periods, labeling noise, and dating errors near the cutoff. The cited passages are labeled as DISTANCE_TRAVEL and only illustrate the construct; they are not evidence of a trend. Conclusion: no robust historical shift.
